title: Nodes get irregularly unuseable
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [x] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [x] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

Hi,

I am not sure if this is the right place to discuss this issue, because it is probably laying in the network stack.
We use OKD 4.14 with OVN Network Layer.

We deployed istio in ambient-mode (we deployed in istio-system, contrary as documented, we use the privileged SCC for istio-system and this is working).

Since one of our customers starts using istio more we do have irregularly node issues. 
First istio-cni starts to get non-ready and furthermore ztunnel because it relies on istio-cni. The node completely  becomes non-reachable via network. No ssh, no debug session possible, no ping, nothing, just dead.

From the logs we cannot see very much, even after we rebooted the node there is not much. With our network team we digged down in OVN, as I am not a Network guy and our network guys are not Kubernetes guys, I try to deliver what we got.

We can see different mangle tables on the nodes, so a node with the issue had this one:

```
        chain ISTIO_OUTPUT {
                ip daddr 169.254.7.127 ip protocol tcp  counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
                ip protocol tcp meta mark & 0x00000fff == 0x00000111 counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
                ip daddr != 127.0.0.1 oifname "lo" counter packets 4549 bytes 273012 accept
                ip daddr != 127.0.0.1 ip protocol tcp meta mark & 0x00000fff != 0x00000539 counter packets 1609715 bytes 96582900 redirect to :15001
        }
```

and other nodes had this one:


```
table ip mangle {
        chain KUBE-IPTABLES-HINT {
        }

        chain KUBE-KUBELET-CANARY {
        }

        chain OVN-KUBE-ITP {
        }

        chain OUTPUT {
                type route hook output priority mangle; policy accept;
                counter packets 122327674 bytes 641811082005 jump OVN-KUBE-ITP
                counter packets 22567146 bytes 178830670492 jump ISTIO_OUTPUT
        }

        chain ISTIO_PRERT {
                meta mark & 0x00000fff == 0x00000539 counter packets 13207 bytes 792420 ct mark set ct mark xor 0x111 and 0xfffff000
                ip saddr 169.254.7.127 ip protocol tcp  counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
                ip daddr != 127.0.0.1 iifname "lo" ip protocol tcp counter packets 1738817 bytes 71798999 accept
                tcp dport 15008 meta mark & 0x00000fff != 0x00000539 counter packets 0 bytes 0 # TPROXY redirect 0.0.0.0:15008 mark 0x111/0xfff
                ip protocol tcp ct state related,established counter packets 1663950 bytes 705867855 accept
                ip daddr != 127.0.0.1 ip protocol tcp meta mark & 0x00000fff != 0x00000539 counter packets 34154 bytes 2049240 # TPROXY redirect 0.0.0.0:15006 mark 0x111/0xfff
        }

        chain ISTIO_OUTPUT {
                ct mark and 0xfff == 0x111 counter packets 64151 bytes 4366280 meta mark set ct mark
        }

        chain PREROUTING {
                type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;
                counter packets 31325649 bytes 424465003964 jump ISTIO_PRERT
        }
}
```

so these differs, probably because the problematic node tried to write iptables rules for the workload on that node.

We already enabled debug logs on istiod, ztunnel and istio-cni with not much information regarding those issues, so I cannot provide any.

We are **not** able to reproducde the issue, this just happens for no reason I can see.

Heres my mesh config:

```
  mesh: |-
    defaultConfig:
      discoveryAddress: istiod.istio-system.svc:15012
      image:
        imageType: distroless
      proxyMetadata:
        ISTIO_META_ENABLE_HBONE: "true"
    defaultProviders:
      metrics:
      - prometheus
    discoverySelectors:
    - matchLabels:
        mycompany/istio-enabled: "true"
    enablePrometheusMerge: true
    rootNamespace: istio-system
    trustDomain: cluster.local
  meshNetworks: 'networks: {}'
```

istio-cni config:

```
data:
  AMBIENT_DNS_CAPTURE: "false"
  AMBIENT_ENABLED: "true"
  AMBIENT_IPV6: "true"
  CHAINED_CNI_PLUGIN: "false"
  CNI_CONF_NAME: istio-cni.conf

  REPAIR_INIT_CONTAINER_NAME: istio-validation
  REPAIR_LABEL_PODS: "false"
  REPAIR_REPAIR_PODS: "true"
```


As I said I am not sure if this is a istio related issue, but it happened since we use more istio workloads.

I am kinda lost where to look.

To "fix" the issue temporarly we drain the node and reboot. Well, this leads of course to some action as the pods needs to get scheduled onto another node. 

Any hint where to look into? 

Thanks!

comments.body:
Hmm, this looks like we install iptables rules that are intended for the pod network namespace into the host. A few possible causes of this...

* We get confused and get a netns file that points to the host network instead of a pod network. An example that could cause this is if we tried to enroll a hostNetwork pod. We _should_ be skipping these but plausibly a bug in that area
* We get the correct netns file, but our invariants in https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/8a89fd6047ab3a9f756372c52f7c7fedaf2f9ce0/tools/istio-iptables/pkg/dependencies/implementation_linux.go#L132 are violated (i.e. run a Go routine which moves us to a new thread not in the netns we wanted)

I noticed you are on 1.23. I strongly recommend 1.24, which is the first GA release. While I never saw this specific bug before, we have fixed a number of bugs in this area since 1.23; plausibly this is one of them

cc @participant2

We can see that every single pod follows this pattern, of having `4026531840` + another network. A single pod, keycloak, has only the `4026531840` entry. Presumably, this `4026531840` is the host network namespace

In typical functioning all pods in a process run within a single network namespace. It is possible to change this, though
* `unshare --map-root-user --net` can make a new network namespace for this pod, without privileges (though some seccomp rules deny this)
* `nsenter --net=/host/proc/1/ns/net` can enter the _host network_ from a pod, but you need a host mount which requires privileges.

I was able to reproduce similar issues with these commands. In the first case, we just fail to setup the config since we put it in the dummy. In the latter, we break the node like you experienced.

The thing I don't get is -- there is a near-zero chance each of those workloads is messing with network namespaces (they don't have permissions to and why would some random application do so), but I don't get what else could do it. Even if we consider some networking tools (OVN, etc) doing weird things, I wouldn't expect them to behave like this. I also looked through OVN source code and tried to install it locally (in kind) and didn't reproduce.

Regarding hostnetwork pods: these should just be entirely excluded from interception, so I don't think its the issue there. Its a non-hostNetwork pod, that somehow has an associated process that is in the host network namespace. Note 'associated' here means it is within the pod's cgroup

I think I am going to give up on reproducing but I think we have enough info to show the proposed fix is _not_ going to be sufficient.

Typical containerd setup:
```
proc1 /pause netns=Pod
proc2 user-command nets=Pod
```

CRI-O setup:
```
proc1 conmon netns=Host
proc2 user-command netns=Pod
```

So if we pick the oldest on CRI-O it will just make us always use the host net.

We could do "oldest non-host netns" since we should know the host netns inode. This wouldn't fix `unshare/nsenter` [cases](https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/55139#issuecomment-2667162362) for CRI-O, but that is a pretty major edge case; along with the non-host netns check it would also mean we could only end up programming the wrong netns but not the host specifically.
